scope: Fresh automated PCI QEMU acceptance against the current worktree ISO. Covers GrModels Man and Ball, KeepAway gameplay/input/Escape, Titanium controls, and broad GUI/runtime regressions. This run does not include the three-minute KeepAway observation. UTM virtio-ramfb and Pi hardware are not covered.
framebuffer_fix: Treat direct framebuffer presentation as active only while text.is_fb_busy is set and text.fb_alias points to the dedicated direct surface. A stale direct-active flag had caused the host to present an all-white direct surface after the alias returned to the compositor buffer.

previous_keepaway_full_run.result: The scanout differed at the periodic samples across the 183-second observation; the game remained responsive through the final sample and Escape returned to a working terminal. The separate live UTM freeze report remains unresolved.

GrModels.Man: pass: form accepted, 112 vertices and 168 triangles; drawing pixels verified; repeat prompt and terminal recovery passed
GrModels.Ball: pass: form accepted, 58 vertices and 128 triangles; inline sprite pixels verified; repeat prompt and terminal recovery passed

KeepAway.gameplay: pass: court/HUD/player rendered; Space and mouse input kept the frame active
KeepAway.long_run: pass: this fresh run observed periodic scanout changes throughout the three-minute gameplay interval; Escape returned to the terminal and 40+2 returned 42.
KeepAway.Escape_recovery: pass: Escape returned to terminal and 40+2 returned 42

Titanium.gameplay: pass: intro and game frame rendered; input and Escape returned to terminal; 40+2 returned 42

live_utm.GrModels: user screenshots show the form and generated vertex count; inline sprite appearance was verified in QEMU but remains visually unconfirmed in UTM
live_utm.KeepAway: still unresolved: QEMU passes on the current ISO, but the user previously reported a full input/display freeze in UTM; this QEMU run does not address the virtio-ramfb difference.
live_utm.Titanium: user-confirmed working in UTM, including ordinary Left/Right, Space, and Escape
